title.narrative: Support for IDPs and returned families in Mozambique

description.narrative: By the end of the project’s 6-month period, improve food security and support the recovery and resilience of 500 displaced and host families in Ancuabe and Mecufi district, Cabo Delgado, by addressing acute nutritional needs through the provision of food assistance, restoring livelihoods with agricultural inputs, and enhancing health practices through the dissemination of hygiene messages via local radio and door-to-door outreach.

Mozambique, located in southeastern Africa, continues to face overlapping humanitarian crises, particularly in the northern province of Cabo Delgado. Since 2017, the region has been deeply affected by violence from non-state armed groups (NSAGs), leading to widespread insecurity, loss of livelihoods, and large-scale displacement. According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), as of April 2024, approximately 945,000 individuals have been displaced within Cabo Delgado, exacerbating existing vulnerabilities for both displaced and host communities.
The humanitarian situation was further worsened in December 2024 by Cyclone Chido, which brought extensive destruction to Cabo Delgado, including the districts of Mecufi, Chiure, Metuge, Ancuabe, Namuno, Montepuez, and Balama. Preliminary reports from the National Institute for Disaster Management (INGD) indicate that thousands of households have lost their homes, crops, and vital assets, leaving them without access to food, shelter, or basic services. The cyclone’s impact has compounded the ongoing conflict-related crises, further intensifying food insecurity and undermining recovery efforts.

Total beneficiaries: 2,500 people
Women: 1,000
